samples.summary: Tab/Shift-Tab reach line indentation through `indentWithTab` without the new same-container guard in `shift()`
samples.evidence: The delta hardens `shift()` (packages/notes/src/view/list-commands.ts:323-334) so a selected list line in a different blockquote depth is never pushed in — the stated hazard is that four columns turn the item into a code block. But Tab is bound in `editor.ts:369/372` to `indentWithTab` from `@codemirror/commands`, which runs the generic `indentMore` over every selected line, with no knowledge of quote depth, list markers or the item above. A multi-line selection spanning `- b` and `>   - c` pressed with Tab still gets the very shift the new guard exists to prevent (and inserts columns in front of the `>` prefix rather than inside the quote). Pre-existing entry point, but this delta is what establishes the invariant it violates; if the invariant matters, Tab should route through `indentList`/`outdentList` (or at least through a list-aware wrapper) rather than raw `indentMore`.

samples.summary: Task/spec doc still states the superseded contract "stop when the neighbouring line's quote prefix differs" / "same prefix = same list"
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260827-notes-blockquote-lists-todo.md:33-35 requires `itemAbove`/`parentOf` to "stop when the neighbouring line's quote prefix differs", and line 65 scopes non-goals as "beyond 'same prefix = same list'". This delta deliberately replaces prefix-text comparison with `quoteDepth()` (list-commands.ts:143-145,159,173), so `>` vs `> ` and `>>` vs `> > ` are now the same container. docs/design/notes/notes.md:796-799 was already updated to say "change of quote depth"; the task doc is the one left describing the old contract and will mislead the next reader of these acceptance criteria.

samples.summary: `toggleQuote`'s divergent QUOTE_RE now underpins container identity used by `quoteDepth`
samples.evidence: `packages/notes/src/view/commands.ts:278` defines its own `QUOTE_RE = /^\s*>\s?/` (unbounded leading whitespace, one level only), while list-commands uses `^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+` and now derives block-container identity from it via `quoteDepth()`. The Quote button can therefore produce/leave prefixes that list-commands classifies at a different depth than the Quote button believes (e.g. a line with 4+ leading spaces before `>` is "quoted" to `toggleQuote` but depth 0 to list-commands, and unquoting a `> > ` line strips only one level), so the two features' notions of "which blockquote is this line in" can disagree. Fix belongs in whichever module should own a shared quote parser; I could not construct a concrete corrupting sequence, hence low confidence.
